page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m1.large is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the shared burstable t6 family. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing two burstable vCPUs mapped to one physical core across two hardware threads. The instance features a 1:1 compute-to-memory ratio, equipped with 2.0 GB of RAM. Instruction set support includes AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI extensions. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes reflect its burstable nature and modest hardware allocation, placing the server predominantly in the bottom percentiles across standard evaluation suites. In stress-ng testing, single-core and multi-core outputs registered 1255.78 and 2507.5 respectively, placing in the bottom 25%. PassMark metrics mirror this profile, with overall CPU performance scoring 2938.6 and memory scoring 880.99. Memory bandwidth reaches 20.37 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 15.46 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific measurements show 2.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its minimal resource footprint, ecs.t6-c1m1.large delivers cost efficiency primarily for low-utilization scenarios where hardware overhead must be kept low. However, the burstable CPU allocation and tight 2.0 GB memory limit make it susceptible to resource constraints under sustained load. The instance is suited for low-traffic web serving, development environments, testing microservices, lightweight utilities, and low-priority task processing.

Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, providing 2 burstable vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 2.0 GB of system memory. The server has no bundled local storage, no GPU hardware, and a baseline network bandwidth profile of 0 Gbps. Empirical benchmark tests reflect its entry-tier allocation, scoring 2938.6 in PassMark CPU tests, 2507.5 in stress-ng multi-core tests, and achieving 2.88 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 20.37 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads. Due to constrained memory and burstable CPU scheduling, it offers a budget-conscious solution appropriate for dev/test environments, lightweight background tasks, low-traffic web serving, and basic utilities.
